subject: Premium Support SKU floor & response ladder — structuring negotiation
messages:
From: Cynthia Ramos <cynthia.ramos@brightgrid.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightgrid.com
Date: Fri, 16 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on premium support packaging

Hi Neha / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the Dedicated cluster performance looks promising for our inference workloads. Before we get into formal procurement, procurement and finance have a couple of questions about the premium support SKU you mentioned:

- Is there a minimum SKU floor / monthly retainer for the Premium Response bundle? Our budget team is sensitive to committed minimums.
- How do uptime tiers map to credits? We need concrete examples (99.95 -> X credits; 99.9 -> Y credits) we can show our SREs.
- Do credits roll forward or are they applied as account credits only (no refunds)?
- For pilot customers, is there an option for a time-limited trial with reduced floor?

If you can send a short spreadsheet and sample SLA wording we can circulate internally. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call this week if easier.

Thanks,
Cynthia Ramos
Director, Platform Engineering
BrightGrid

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 May 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on premium support packaging

Cynthia — thanks for the clear list. Attached are two items: a draft SLA (BrightGrid_SLA_Draft_v2.pdf) and a short response-ladder spreadsheet (response-ladder-sheet.xlsx) that maps uptime bands to credit percentages. High level answers below; happy to sync.

- Minimum SKU floor: our standard Premium Response retainer starts at $5,000/mo for self-service startups. We can annualize and true-up versus committed spend.
- Uptime->credits: see spreadsheet but quick examples: 99.95% = 5% monthly credit; 99.9% = 10% monthly credit (sliding scale tied to minutes of unavailability).
- Credit mechanics: credits apply to invoices (no cash refunds). Credits can be banked for up to 6 months for pilot customers; for enterprise commits we support longer accruals or invoice-level refunds on a case-by-case basis.
- Pilot options: we typically offer a 3-month pilot at a reduced floor (50% of SKU floor) that converts to a committed SKU at the end of the pilot with a one-time onboarding discount.

If you can share expected monthly request volume and whether you'll be using Dedicated pools, I can propose two concrete pricing scenarios (pilot -> committed).

Neha Kapoor

Subject: Re: Quick question on premium support packaging

Adding some price-structuring context from the ops side — thanks for the question, Cynthia. A few negotiation levers we've used successfully with infra teams:

- Volume tiers: reduce SKU floor at higher committed spend bands (e.g., $5k floor < $100k ARR, $3k floor < $50k ARR when annualized).
- Onboarding discount: 10–15% credit on month 1 for pilots that convert.
- Escalation coverage: include a base level of 24x7 escalation for Severity 1 incidents; additional named SRE support can be added as a time-and-materials overlay or via a small retainer.
- Credit granularity: break the SLA into micro-windows (e.g., 15 min increments) to keep credit math predictable.

I'll model two scenarios once we get your volume numbers: 1) 3-month pilot (50% floor) -> convert to annual commit with 10% onboarding credit; 2) pilot converts to a quarterly committed cadence with a sliding floor. Both include an escalation playbook and a mutual action plan.

Marissa
Director, Customer Solutions
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Quick question on premium support packaging

Thanks Neha / Marissa — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement:

- BrightGrid procurement prefers a SKU floor closer to $3k/mo for pilots (our finance team treats the floor as a recurring operating expense). Can you support $3k for the 3-month pilot instead of 50% of $5k?
- Instead of credits only, procurement asked whether we can structure a partial refund if uptime drops below 99.5% for two consecutive months — they want to avoid credits sitting unused.
- We’d like the pilot to be cancellable at 30 days with pro-rated billing if it’s not meeting SLAs.

We can do a demo with our SREs next Wednesday. Also, can you send a sample DocuSign we can push through procurement?

Best,
Cynthia

Subject: Re: Quick question on premium support packaging

Neha / Marissa — happy to weigh in. Given BrightGrid's profile (likely Dedicated usage and predictable growth), I can approve a constrained exception to standard floors to help close the pilot:

- Pilot SKU floor: set to $4,000/mo for a 3-month pilot (split-billed monthly).
- Onboarding concession: 10% credit on first invoice if pilot converts to an annual commit within 45 days of pilot end.
- Refund carve: for two consecutive months below 99.5% we agree to either a credit or a one-time invoice-level refund up to 20% of that month's retainer (procurement choice).
- Cancellation: pilot cancellable with 30-day notice; any prorated credits apply.

I'll ask Legal to add a short clause allowing invoice-level refunds for that specific condition; otherwise credits remain the default. If procurement insists on refunds more broadly we may need a risk review.

Jonas Weber
VP, Customer Success (acting)
